# Independent audit: contact martingales and global parameter optimality

Audited source:
`candidate b2578378c7102b3c`,
Sections 1--6. Result: **PASS**, with no substantive repair.

This is an analytic proof audit. The finite-source transport dependency is
the already independently audited
`candidate 3b257d8ddacb6167`.
The actual buffer step additionally uses Section 3 of
`candidate 5f79e6103cd27dac`.
Its fixed positive epsilon, positive fibers, interior marked source, and
fixed mass/covariance normalization remain in force. In particular, the
strictness statement would not be asserted for epsilon=0.

## 1. The row reweighting and finite inequality

The measures rho_i in the source are probability laws; their coefficients
sigma_i/L_i need not sum to one. Concave-L contact gives
E_rho L=L_i, so bar-rho_i=(L/L_i)rho_i is a probability. The target identity
then gives exactly sum sigma_i bar-rho_i=dm/M, without an unproved uniform
fiber lift or a replacement of its true continuous marginal.

For any positive continuous concave U, let R=U/L. The actual martingale
mean E_rho w=Y_i gives

    E_bar-rho R = E_rho U/L_i <= U(Y_i)/L_i = R_i.

One must use the rho mean here; the bar-rho mean is generally different.
Applying logarithmic Jensen to bar-rho proves the displayed global
inequality. Compactness and strict positivity of U,L bound every density
ratio away from zero and infinity, so every logarithm and relative
entropy in the proof is finite. No passage through a derivative or a
moving polyhedral cell is required.

## 2. Exact deficit and sampled rigidity

With b_i=E_bar-rho R and tau_i=(R/b_i)bar-rho_i,

    KL(bar-rho_i || tau_i)=log b_i-E_bar-rho_i log R.

Thus the claimed gap is exactly the sum of two separately nonnegative
terms. Zero entropy forces R=b_i almost surely, and the other zero term
forces b_i=R_i. The converse is immediate. This verifies both necessity
and sufficiency of the stated equality conditions.

For normalized U satisfying U(Y_i)<=L_i at every positive source, the
global right-hand side is zero and every logarithm on the left is
nonpositive. Therefore all source ratios equal one and all row entropy
gaps vanish. The full target identity then gives U=L m-almost everywhere.
Continuity upgrades this to the whole of each sampled positive fiber:
every relative-open neighborhood, including one meeting its boundary,
has positive d-volume. Equality between the sampled fibers is correctly
not claimed.

The auxiliary maximization of integral log U under the finitely many
marked upper bounds also follows directly from the same inequality. Its
uniqueness is modulo the actual measure, precisely as stated.

## 3. Complete radial directions include moving planes

If h+cL is concave, applying the row inequality to h+cL and subtracting
the exactly equal L moments proves the claimed linear dual. Conversely,
both signs of affine functions belong to this cone, giving mass and
first moments; negatives of continuous convex functions give convex
order. The cited finite-source allocation proof then produces actual
rows, and equality of summed L moments gives every row contact.

For an exact positive concave competitor L_t, its secant
h_t=(L_t-L)/t has h_t+L/t=L_t/t concave. Thus every such finite change,
including switches of the planes in min_r(A_r+t B_r), is already tested
by the radial cone. Uniform differentiability on a crease is irrelevant.
This does not claim that every formal infinitesimal plane motion has a
uniform derivative; it avoids needing that assertion.

## 4. Proper-gap strict monotonicity, with the attained new cap

Fix a source w=(p,y) with scalar buffer delta_0>0 and raw depth Q_0
strictly less than its pure-base depth b. Let delta_1>delta_0 and denote
its new depth by Q_1. Monotonicity gives Q_1>=Q_0 and always Q_1<=b.
If Q_1=b, strictness follows from Q_0<b. Otherwise the proper-gap
attainment theorem supplies an ACTUAL minimizing cap at delta_1 with
nonzero continuous normal and a proper own-fiber threshold.

At the same normal and base tilt, changing delta_1 to delta_0 raises the
threshold by a strictly positive amount. Because the new threshold lies
strictly between the own-fiber support extrema, this removes positive
own d-volume, even if the shift later passes the far support. All other
fiber losses are nonnegative. Consequently

    Q_0 <= mass of this cap at delta_0
         < mass of this cap at delta_1 = Q_1.

This is the required strictness. It uses the attained NEW minimizer;
following only an old critical cut would not suffice. Proper closed cuts
have zero boundary d-volume. No regularity of supporting cuts in other
fibers, fixed active menu, or differentiability of the cap minimum is
inserted.

## 5. The actual global parameter conclusion

The multiplicative inequality provides a positive source i with
U(Y_i)>=L_i. With bodies, M, covariance norm, and positive epsilon fixed,
the scalar buffer at this mark increases monotonically with that value.
Therefore its new depth is at least Q, proving global parameter
optimality of L.

If U has global maximum at most Q, the strictness in Section 4 forbids
U(Y_i)>L_i for ANY positive source. Section 2 then forces equality on
every sampled fiber. Thus global uniqueness has exactly the sampled
restriction scope asserted by the source. It supplies neither a
body-deformation certificate nor a per-label Gamma bound. The existing
one-gradient class-payment obstruction remains compatible with it.

All section formulas, logical quantifiers, and equality implications
check. No additional hidden first-order condition from moving planes
survives outside the tested exact secants.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
